To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

metagenomics is a useful tool for the detection of viruses and the establishment of a causal relationship between a virus and disease, but that this approach should be used with caution, especially when the disease is not very common or has a low mortality rate.

the metagenomic discovery of novel viruses is a powerful tool for understanding the role of viruses in the etiology of human diseases, but the criteria for establishing causality are not yet fully developed.
the metagenomic discovery of new viruses can help to establish causality between a virus and the disease it causes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery and characterization of new viruses in the environment and in biological samples.
the study of the role of viruses in human diseases and their discovery in the environment.
the study of the viral diversity and their role in the environment and in human health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a virus is the cause of a disease when the following criteria are fulfilled: (i) the virus is consistently present in the diseased tissues, (ii) the virus can be isolated in culture and can induce disease in susceptible animals, and (iii) the virus is eliminated by specific antiviral treatment or immunization.
“the virus is present in the disease, the virus is associated to the disease, the presence of the virus precedes the disease and the removal of the virus leads to the resolution of the disease”.

a virus is the causative agent of a disease if it is demonstrated to be present at high titer in all patients with the disease and in no healthy individuals, and it can be experimentally transmitted to healthy individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are still in the early stage of a revolution in virology, which is being driven by the metagenomic approaches and the new sequencing technologies.
the discovery of new viral agents by metagenomic approaches is not a simple task.
the metagenomic method is a powerful tool to identify new viruses, however, the causality of the disease must be proven by other means.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a causal association between the virus and disease should be established by using a combination of epidemiological, virological and clinical data.
the metagenomic data should be used to complement the classical epidemiological approach, and not to replace it.

metagenomic approaches are very powerful for the discovery of new virus species and for understanding viral ecology, but the etiological role of the viruses found in these studies should be carefully investigated.
